title: A square of quasi-isomorphisms induces a quasi-isomorphism of cones
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], and use integer cochain complexes, cohomology, shifts, cones and quasi-isomorphisms as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $u:K\to L$ and $u':K'\to L'$ be chain maps, and let $s:K\to K'$ and $t:L\to L'$ be quasi-isomorphisms satisfying $t\circ u=u'\circ s$. The diagonal cone map
$$c:\operatorname{Cone}(u)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Cone}(u'),\qquad c^n=\begin{pmatrix}t^n&0\\0&s^{n+1}\end{pmatrix},$$
is a quasi-isomorphism. More precisely, the canonical degreewise split sequences $0\to L\to\operatorname{Cone}(u)\to K[1]\to0$ and $0\to L'\to\operatorname{Cone}(u')\to K'[1]\to0$ are carried one to the other by $(t,c,s[1])$, and these maps give a morphism of their long exact cohomology sequences, including the connecting morphisms. No boundedness or termwise flatness hypothesis is required.
